questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The site operation involving the formal transfer of a construction site from the client/consultant to the contractor is called
questions.explanation: Handing over marks the formal transfer of the site and relevant documentation to the contractor before construction work begins.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The site operation involving the removal of trees, bushes, and debris to prepare land for construction is called
questions.explanation: Site clearing removes vegetation, trees, and debris to prepare a clear, workable area before construction begins.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The site operation involving the adjustment of ground surfaces to a required uniform gradient is called
questions.explanation: Levelling adjusts the ground to the required elevation and gradient in preparation for building works.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The temporary protective fencing or boarding erected around a construction site to restrict public access is called
questions.explanation: Hoarding is a temporary barrier erected around a site to prevent unauthorised access and protect the public from construction hazards.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The process of transferring the exact position and dimensions of a proposed building from the drawing onto the actual ground is called
questions.explanation: Setting out translates the building's design dimensions and position from the drawings onto the physical site, guiding excavation and construction.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Temporary boards fixed at the corners of a building site, used to hold reference lines (profiles) during setting out, are called
questions.explanation: Profile boards, positioned beyond the excavation area, hold string lines marking the building's exact corners and wall positions.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The construction method using a 3:4:5 ratio of side lengths to accurately establish a 90-degree right angle on site is called the
questions.explanation: The 3:4:5 method uses the Pythagorean relationship (3² + 4² = 5²) to construct an accurate right angle using simple measuring tape and pegs.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Checking that the diagonals of a rectangular building layout are equal in length is done primarily to confirm
options: the type of soil present on site
the total area of the building
that the building's corners are square (at right angles)
questions.explanation: Equal diagonal measurements in a rectangular layout confirm that all four corners are true right angles, verifying the layout's squareness.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The process of digging a narrow, elongated excavation to receive a strip foundation is called
questions.explanation: Trench excavation creates the narrow channel needed to accommodate a strip foundation beneath a building's walls.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Temporary timber supports used to prevent the collapse of trench walls during excavation, especially in loose soil, are called
questions.explanation: Timbering (shoring) supports the sides of an excavation to prevent collapse, particularly critical in loose or unstable soil conditions.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: In firm, stable soils, the amount of timbering required to support a trench is generally
options: less than in loose or unstable soils
the same as in loose soils regardless of stability
questions.explanation: Firm, cohesive soils are more self-supporting, generally requiring less extensive timbering compared to loose, unstable, or sandy soils.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The binding building material produced by heating limestone and clay, then grinding the resulting clinker into a fine powder, is called
questions.explanation: Cement is manufactured by heating limestone and clay to form clinker, which is then finely ground, and acts as the binding agent in concrete and mortar.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A concrete mix ratio of 1:2:4 typically refers to the proportions of
questions.explanation: A 1:2:4 mix ratio specifies one part cement, two parts sand (fine aggregate), and four parts coarse aggregate by volume.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The test used to assess the workability (consistency) of freshly mixed concrete before it sets is called the
questions.explanation: The slump test measures how much a sample of fresh concrete settles under its own weight, indicating its workability for placement.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Building blocks manufactured from a mixture of cement, sand, and aggregate, cast and cured to a standard size, are called
questions.explanation: Concrete blocks are manufactured from a cement-sand-aggregate mixture, cast into standard shapes and cured before use in construction.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Building units manufactured from moulded and fired clay, traditionally used for wall construction, are called
questions.explanation: Bricks are made from clay, shaped and fired at high temperatures to produce durable units for building construction.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Metals such as iron and steel, which contain iron as their main constituent, are classified as
questions.explanation: Ferrous metals contain iron as a primary constituent, distinguishing them from non-ferrous metals like aluminium and copper.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Metals such as aluminium, copper, and zinc, which do not contain iron as their main constituent, are classified as
questions.explanation: Non-ferrous metals lack iron as a primary constituent, generally offering advantages such as corrosion resistance compared to ferrous metals.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Waterproofing products such as bitumen and asphalt, used to protect building elements from moisture penetration, are classified as
questions.explanation: Bituminous products, derived from petroleum, provide effective waterproofing for roofs, foundations, and other building elements.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Sand and gravel used as filler materials in concrete, providing bulk and strength, are collectively known as
questions.explanation: Aggregates (sand and gravel/crushed stone) form the bulk of concrete, with cement acting as the binding agent holding them together.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Synthetic materials, such as PVC pipes and plastic sheeting, increasingly used in modern construction for their durability and low cost, are classified as
questions.explanation: Plastics are widely used in modern construction for applications such as piping, insulation, and sheeting, valued for durability and cost-effectiveness.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A concrete mix ratio of 1:3:6 is generally used for applications requiring
options: lower strength, such as mass concrete or blinding layers
the highest possible structural strength, such as suspended beams
questions.explanation: A leaner 1:3:6 mix, with less cement relative to aggregate, is typically used for lower-strength applications such as blinding layers or mass concrete fill.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Glass used in building construction, such as for windows, is valued mainly for its
options: transparency, allowing natural light into a building
high compressive strength for structural columns
questions.explanation: Glass is primarily valued in construction for its transparency, allowing daylight to enter a building while providing weather protection.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Timber used in building construction requires proper seasoning (drying) mainly to
options: reduce its moisture content and minimise shrinkage or warping after installation
increase its weight for structural stability
eliminate the need for any further treatment against pests
questions.explanation: Seasoning timber reduces its moisture content before use, minimising the risk of shrinkage, warping, or splitting once installed in a building.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The part of a building structure below ground level, transferring the building's load safely to the supporting soil, is called the
questions.explanation: The foundation (substructure) transfers the entire load of a building safely into the ground, and its design depends on soil bearing capacity.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The maximum load per unit area that a soil can safely support without excessive settlement or failure is called its
questions.explanation: Soil bearing capacity determines how much load the ground can safely carry, directly influencing foundation design and depth.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A continuous foundation running beneath load-bearing walls, typically used for simple building structures, is called a
questions.explanation: Strip foundations run continuously beneath load-bearing walls, distributing the wall's load evenly along its length into the ground.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A foundation consisting of individual, separate concrete bases supporting isolated columns is called a
questions.explanation: Pad (isolated) footings support individual columns separately, rather than running continuously as with strip foundations.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A foundation consisting of a single continuous concrete slab covering the entire building area, used especially on weak or variable soils, is called a
questions.explanation: A raft (mat) foundation spreads the building's total load over a large continuous slab, useful on weak or variable soil conditions.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A foundation using long columns driven or bored deep into the ground to reach stable, load-bearing strata, is called a
questions.explanation: Pile foundations transfer building loads deep into the ground to reach strong, stable soil or rock layers, especially useful where surface soils are weak.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Broken stones or rubble laid and compacted as a base layer beneath a ground floor slab is called
questions.explanation: Hardcore consists of compacted broken stone or rubble, providing a stable, well-drained base layer beneath a floor slab.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A thin layer of fine sand spread over hardcore to fill surface voids before laying a damp-proof membrane is called
questions.explanation: Sand blinding fills the surface irregularities of a hardcore layer, providing a smoother base for the damp-proof membrane above.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A waterproof sheet material laid beneath a ground floor slab to prevent rising moisture from the ground is called a
questions.explanation: The damp-proof membrane (DPM) is a waterproof layer that prevents ground moisture from rising into the floor slab and building interior.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The concrete layer cast directly on top of the hardcore, sand blinding, and damp-proof membrane to form the ground floor base is called the
questions.explanation: The oversite concrete bed forms the solid ground floor base, cast over the prepared hardcore, sand blinding, and damp-proof membrane layers.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A key factor considered when selecting the appropriate foundation type for a building is the
options: soil bearing capacity and ground conditions at the site
type of roof covering to be used
number of paint coats to be applied
colour of the building's exterior finish
questions.explanation: Foundation selection depends heavily on the site's soil conditions and bearing capacity, ensuring the chosen foundation can safely support the building's loads.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Pile foundations are generally preferred over shallow foundations when
options: the soil near the surface has poor bearing capacity, requiring loads to be transferred to deeper, stronger strata
the surface soil already has excellent bearing capacity
cost is the only consideration, regardless of soil conditions
the building is very light and single-storey
questions.explanation: Piles are chosen when surface soils cannot adequately support a building's loads, allowing the load to be transferred down to deeper, more stable soil or rock layers.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The width of a strip foundation is primarily determined by
options: the load of the wall above and the bearing capacity of the supporting soil
the colour of the finished wall
the number of windows in the building
the type of roof to be constructed
questions.explanation: Strip foundation width is calculated to ensure the load from the wall above is spread over a sufficient area of ground, based on the soil's bearing capacity.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Before casting the oversite concrete bed, it is important to first ensure that the hardcore layer is
options: installed after the concrete has already been cast
well compacted and blinded with sand to provide an even surface
questions.explanation: Proper compaction and sand blinding of the hardcore layer provides a stable, even base, preventing settlement issues beneath the finished floor slab.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A raft foundation is often chosen over a strip or pad foundation mainly to
options: spread the building's load over a wide area on weak or variable soil conditions
increase the depth of excavation required unnecessarily
eliminate the need for a damp-proof membrane
reduce the overall cost of excavation in all soil types
questions.explanation: Raft foundations distribute a building's total load across a large continuous area, making them particularly suitable for weak or inconsistent soil conditions.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A wall designed to carry and transfer structural loads from the roof and floors down to the foundation is called a
questions.explanation: Load-bearing walls support and transfer structural loads from above down through the wall to the foundation.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A wall used only to divide internal spaces, without carrying any structural load from the building above, is called a
questions.explanation: Non-load-bearing (partition) walls simply divide interior spaces and do not support structural loads from the building above.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A common brickwork bond in which each brick is laid so that only its shorter end (header) is not visible, showing mostly the long face (stretcher), is called the
questions.explanation: Stretcher bond shows the long face (stretcher) of each brick in every course, one of the simplest and most common bonding patterns.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A brickwork bond alternating complete courses of headers and complete courses of stretchers is called the
questions.explanation: English bond alternates whole courses of headers with whole courses of stretchers, producing a strong, traditional bonding pattern.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A brickwork bond alternating headers and stretchers within each individual course is called the
questions.explanation: Flemish bond alternates headers and stretchers within the same course, producing a distinctive decorative pattern while maintaining structural strength.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A structural member placed above a door or window opening to support the wall load above it is called a
questions.explanation: A lintel spans across an opening, such as a door or window, transferring the load of the wall above safely to the sides.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A curved structural member spanning an opening, transferring load through compression along its curve, is called an
questions.explanation: An arch spans an opening using a curved shape, transferring loads through compression down to its supporting piers.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A vertical structural member that transfers loads from beams or slabs down to the foundation is called a
questions.explanation: Columns are vertical members that carry loads from beams, slabs, or roofs, transferring them down to the foundation.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A continuous impervious layer built into a wall at plinth level, preventing rising dampness from entering the wall above ground, is called the
questions.explanation: The damp-proof course (DPC) is installed within the wall at plinth level to block rising ground moisture from penetrating higher into the structure.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A floor constructed using timber joists supporting floorboards, common in some residential upper floors, is called a
questions.explanation: Timber floors use joists to support floorboards, a lightweight construction method commonly used for upper floors in residential buildings.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A floor constructed as a continuous cast reinforced concrete slab, without hollow blocks or ribs, is called a
questions.explanation: A solid concrete slab floor is cast as one continuous reinforced concrete section, without internal voids.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A reinforced concrete floor incorporating hollow blocks (pots) between concrete ribs to reduce weight and material use is called a
questions.explanation: Hollow pot (ribbed) floors incorporate lightweight hollow blocks between structural concrete ribs, reducing the overall weight and material cost of the floor.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A hard-wearing floor finish made from marble or granite chips set in cement or resin and polished smooth is called
questions.explanation: Terrazzo is a durable, decorative flooring finish made from marble or granite chips set in a binder and polished to a smooth surface.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A thin layer of mortar applied over a concrete floor to provide a smooth, level surface for further finishing is called
questions.explanation: Screeding applies a thin, level mortar layer over a concrete floor base, preparing it for the final floor finish.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A temporary structure erected around a building to provide access and support for workers and materials during construction is called
questions.explanation: Scaffolding provides safe temporary access and working platforms for construction workers at various heights around a building.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Scaffolding erected independently of the building, supported entirely by its own vertical and horizontal members without relying on the wall, is called
questions.explanation: Independent scaffolding stands entirely on its own structural framework, without needing support from the building under construction.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Scaffolding partly supported by inserting horizontal tubes (putlogs) directly into the joints of the building's wall as it is constructed is called
questions.explanation: Putlog scaffolding relies partly on the building itself for support, with putlog tubes resting in specially left joints within the rising wall.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The vertical tubes in a scaffold structure that transfer load down to the ground are called
questions.explanation: Standards are the vertical scaffold tubes that bear the overall load and transfer it safely down to the ground.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The horizontal tubes in a scaffold structure that connect the standards together, running parallel to the building, are called
questions.explanation: Ledgers are horizontal scaffold tubes connecting standards together, running parallel to the face of the building.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The horizontal tubes in a scaffold structure that span across the ledgers, supporting the scaffold boards, are called
questions.explanation: Transoms span across the ledgers at right angles, providing the direct support for the scaffold's working boards.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A temporary mould constructed to hold wet concrete in place until it gains sufficient strength to be self-supporting is called
questions.explanation: Formwork (shuttering) temporarily contains and shapes wet concrete for elements such as columns, beams, and slabs until the concrete cures.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: In stair terminology, the horizontal surface of a step on which a person places their foot is called the
questions.explanation: The tread is the horizontal top surface of a stair step, providing the walking surface for each step.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: In stair terminology, the vertical surface between two consecutive treads is called the
questions.explanation: The riser is the vertical face of a stair step, connecting one tread to the next.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: In stair terminology, the horizontal distance measured from the face of one riser to the face of the next is called the
questions.explanation: The going measures the horizontal distance between successive risers, an important dimension in stair design.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: In stair terminology, the small projecting edge of a tread that overhangs the riser below is called the
questions.explanation: The nosing is the projecting front edge of a tread, extending slightly over the riser beneath it, often to improve grip and appearance.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: In stair terminology, the angle of inclination of a staircase relative to the horizontal is called the
questions.explanation: The pitch describes the angle at which a staircase is inclined, an important consideration for comfort and safety of use.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: In stair terminology, the vertical clearance distance between a stair tread and the ceiling or structure above it is called the
questions.explanation: Headroom is the vertical clearance above a stair, ensuring users have adequate space to walk without striking their head.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A roof design with a single sloping surface, often built against an existing wall, is called a
questions.explanation: A lean-to roof has a single sloping surface, typically leaning against an existing higher wall or structure.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A roof design with two sloping surfaces meeting at a ridge, with triangular vertical wall sections (gables) at each end, is called a
questions.explanation: A gable roof has two sloping sides meeting at a central ridge, with the triangular gable ends visible at either side.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A roof design with sloping surfaces on all four sides, meeting at a ridge, without vertical gable ends, is called a
questions.explanation: A hip roof slopes on all four sides, converging at a central ridge, without the vertical triangular gable ends seen in gable roofs.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A roof design combining two different slopes on each side, with the lower slope steeper than the upper, is called a
questions.explanation: A mansard roof has two distinct slopes on each side, with a steeper lower slope and a shallower upper slope, often maximising usable attic space.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The horizontal timber member fixed along the top of a wall, providing a level base to which the roof structure is fixed, is called the
questions.explanation: The wall plate is a horizontal timber fixed along the top of a wall, distributing the roof's load evenly and providing an anchor point for rafters.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The sloping timber members running from the wall plate to the ridge, forming the main structural framework of a pitched roof, are called
questions.explanation: Common rafters are the sloping structural members running from the wall plate up to the ridge, forming the roof's basic skeleton.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A horizontal timber member providing intermediate support to rafters along their length, reducing the span they must cover unsupported, is called a
questions.explanation: Purlins run horizontally across rafters, providing intermediate support that reduces the unsupported span of the rafters.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The central vertical member in a traditional timber roof truss, supporting the ridge and transferring load down to the tie beam, is called the
questions.explanation: The king post is the central vertical member of a traditional roof truss, connecting the ridge to the tie beam and helping to carry the roof's load.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A prefabricated triangulated framework used to support a roof's structure over a wide span is called a
questions.explanation: A truss is a triangulated framework, often prefabricated, designed to efficiently support a roof over a wide span.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A common lightweight roof covering material made from corrugated metal or fibre-cement sheets is called
questions.explanation: Corrugated sheets, made from metal or fibre-cement, are a widely used, lightweight, and cost-effective roof covering material.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A door constructed with solid or raised sections framed within stiles and rails, often used for a traditional decorative appearance, is called a
questions.explanation: Panel doors feature raised or recessed panels set within a surrounding timber frame, giving a traditional decorative appearance.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A door with a smooth, flat surface on both sides, typically constructed from a hollow or solid core covered by plywood or hardboard, is called a
questions.explanation: Flush doors have a completely flat, smooth surface, constructed by covering a solid or hollow core with a plywood or hardboard skin.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A simple, traditional door constructed from vertical boards held together by horizontal ledges and diagonal braces is called a
questions.explanation: Ledged and braced doors are made from vertical boards fixed to horizontal ledges and diagonal braces, a simple, sturdy traditional construction.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A window with one or more hinged sashes that open outward or inward like a door is called a
questions.explanation: Casement windows have hinged sashes that swing open, similar to a door, providing good ventilation control.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A window with sashes that move horizontally past each other within a frame, rather than swinging open, is called a
questions.explanation: Sliding windows open by moving one sash horizontally along a track, rather than swinging outward or inward.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A window made up of angled, overlapping glass or metal slats that can be adjusted to control airflow is called a
questions.explanation: Louvre windows consist of adjustable, overlapping slats that can be tilted to control ventilation while providing some weather protection.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Hardware fittings such as hinges, locks, and door handles, used on doors and windows, are collectively known as
questions.explanation: Ironmongery refers to the metal fittings and hardware, such as hinges, locks, and handles, used on doors and windows.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The application of a smooth, protective, and decorative coating of mortar to internal wall surfaces is called
questions.explanation: Plastering applies a smooth mortar finish to internal wall surfaces, providing a suitable base for decoration and additional protection.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The application of a protective and decorative coating of mortar to external wall surfaces is called
questions.explanation: Rendering applies a protective mortar coating to external wall surfaces, improving weather resistance and appearance.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A drainage system specifically designed to collect and dispose of rainwater from roofs and paved surfaces is called the
questions.explanation: Surface water drainage systems collect and dispose of rainwater runoff from roofs, driveways, and other paved surfaces.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A drainage system specifically designed to carry wastewater from toilets and similar sanitary fittings is called the
questions.explanation: Soil water drainage systems carry foul wastewater from toilets and similar fittings away from the building for treatment or disposal.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: An underground tank system that treats sewage on-site where a connection to a public sewer is unavailable is called a
questions.explanation: A septic tank system treats and partially breaks down sewage on-site, commonly used where mains sewer connections are unavailable.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: An underground pit filled with rubble or gravel, allowing treated wastewater or surface water to gradually soak into the surrounding ground, is called a
questions.explanation: A soakaway pit allows water to disperse gradually into the surrounding soil, commonly used alongside septic systems or for surface water disposal.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The protective tubes or channels installed within walls and floors to route electrical wiring safely through a building are called
questions.explanation: Electrical conduits protect and route wiring safely through the walls, floors, and ceilings of a building.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The main purpose of installing a damp-proof course (DPC) at plinth level in a wall is to
options: prevent rising ground moisture from penetrating the wall above ground level
improve the wall's fire resistance rating
increase the compressive strength of the wall
reduce the overall weight of the building
questions.explanation: The DPC forms a continuous impervious barrier within the wall at plinth level, specifically blocking rising damp from travelling further up the structure.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A cavity wall, consisting of two separate wall leaves with an air gap between them, is primarily constructed to
options: eliminate the need for a damp-proof course entirely
reduce the overall foundation depth required
improve resistance to moisture penetration and thermal insulation
questions.explanation: Cavity walls use an air gap between two wall leaves to help prevent moisture penetration to the inner leaf and improve thermal insulation.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A key advantage of reinforced concrete floors over timber floors is their
options: faster construction time in every situation
lower material cost in every situation
questions.explanation: Reinforced concrete floors generally offer superior fire resistance and long-term durability compared to timber floor construction.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The primary purpose of formwork in reinforced concrete construction is to
options: reinforce the concrete against tension forces
contain and shape the wet concrete until it has gained sufficient strength
provide the finished decorative surface texture in every case
questions.explanation: Formwork temporarily holds and shapes wet concrete during casting and early curing, until the concrete is strong enough to support itself.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A key safety consideration when designing a staircase is ensuring consistent
options: decorative pattern on the underside of the stair
tread and riser dimensions throughout the flight, to avoid trip hazards
colour scheme matching the surrounding walls
questions.explanation: Uneven tread or riser dimensions within a single staircase flight create serious trip hazards, so consistency is a key safety requirement in stair design.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The primary function of a roof truss in building construction is to
options: serve as the primary damp-proofing layer
provide the internal partition walls of the building
support the roof covering and transfer its load safely to the supporting walls
questions.explanation: Roof trusses form the structural skeleton that carries the roof covering's load and transfers it safely down to the supporting walls.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: A flat roof design, as opposed to a pitched roof, requires particular attention to
options: effective waterproofing and drainage to prevent water ponding
the use of common rafters exclusively
the installation of a ridge board
questions.explanation: Because flat roofs lack the natural water run-off of a pitched design, they require especially careful waterproofing and drainage design to avoid ponding and leaks.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Ledged and braced doors are generally considered less suitable for external use in exposed conditions mainly because they
options: are always made only from metal
cannot be fitted with any locks or hinges
are more expensive to manufacture than panel doors
can be prone to warping and sagging over time without a rigid perimeter frame
questions.explanation: Without a rigid perimeter frame like a panel door, ledged and braced doors can be more prone to warping or sagging over time, particularly under weather exposure.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: Effective site drainage design for a building plot is important mainly to
options: replace the need for a proper foundation design
increase the overall cost of construction unnecessarily
prevent water accumulation that could damage the foundation or superstructure
eliminate the need for a damp-proof course
questions.explanation: Well-planned site drainage prevents water from accumulating around a building, protecting both the foundation and the superstructure from moisture-related damage.

questions.subject: Building Construction
questions.text: The choice between a gable roof and a hip roof for a building often depends partly on
options: the desired architectural appearance and the building's exposure to wind
the depth of the damp-proof course installed
the colour of the internal wall paint
the type of foundation used beneath the building
questions.explanation: Roof type selection is influenced by both aesthetic preference and practical factors such as wind exposure, since hip roofs can offer better wind resistance than gable roofs.
